newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-I DEEPLY REGRET WHAT HAPPENED - GASCOIGNE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-I DEEPLY REGRET WHAT HAPPENED - GASCOIGNE.

text.p: Paul Gascoigne, speaking for the first time about the day he allegedly beat his wife Sheryl, said on Monday he "deeply regretted what happened".
Gascoigne, preparing for England's World Cup qualifier in Goergia on Saturday, said: "I can't go into great detail about the incident but I deeply regret what happened. It will live with me forever."
England coach Glenn Hoddle caused a storm of public protest when he included the midfielder in his squad despite newspaper revelations of Gascoigne's alleged assault.

Hoddle said when he announced his selection last Friday that his hope was that the Glasgow Rangers and former Tottenham and Lazio midfielder would become a better person when he actually came to terms with his actions.
In the aftermath of the incident, Gascoigne revealed he had decided the following day to seek help for his problems.
"It's hard to talk to a stranger about your problems but I feel a better person for it," he said.
"The counselling has helped me. It's making me relax both on the pitch and off it and I do feel a better person all round.
"At times there's been a rage inside me, something I can't really describe, but that's why I'm taking the counselling.
"What I can say is that it is helping me. I wanted to say something today, to get it across.

"Perhaps it's something I would have benefited from before. Perhaps I've been under more pressure than a lot of people for the past five or six years and I've bottled it all up inside me, instead of letting it come out.
"What happened with Sheryl was the last straw. Now I've started to sort it out and I'm really pleased."
Women's right groups have reacted angrily to Hoddle's decision to select Gascoigne and the player himself indicated he thought they had a right to be angry.
"I don't blame the women's groups for wanting me kicked out of the squad," he admitted.
"They have their right to say that, and in the last week or so leading up to the announcement I didn't think I was going to be in the squad.

"But the next international after this one isn't until February. That would have been an even longer wait. I told Glenn that I wanted to play and I just thank him and the F.A. (English Football Association) for giving me this chance to prove I'm still capable of doing the business for England."
Hoddle said his next decision was whether to select Gascoigne for Saturday's game in Tbilisi.
The manager did add that he now believed Gascoigne would be able to cope with omission from the side but "that will be a footballing decision which we will make when we get out there".
